 Nebraska Wage Hike Reduced as South Dakota Sees Larger Increase for 2027
 November 20 , 2026 2:23 pm by Jett Rasmussen 
 Nebraska State Capitol, Photo by Jett Rasmussen 
 With 2026 coming to a close in just over a month, laborers working by the hour in Nebraska and South Dakota can look forward to a minimum wage increase at the start of 2027 . Nebraska and South Dakota are two of 16 states that will see a wage increase next year.
 For Nebraska, voters passed a law in 2022 allowing a series of annual wage increases based on inflation. However, earlier this year, the Nebraska Legislature passed LB 258 . That bill amends the previous inflation-based adjustment to a fixed 1.75% raise. Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen signed that bill into law in February 2026.
 The actual raise out of that 1.75% figure will be 26 cents. Nebraska’s minimum wage currently sits at $15.00. That will now go up to $15.26. Notably, that is 29 cents less than the expected increase ($15.55) prior to the passage and enactment of LB 258. In other words, a full-time worker (40 hours per week over 52 weeks) would earn nearly $600 less per year at $15.26 than at $15.55, before taxes.
 While South Dakota’s minimum wage is much lower than Nebraska’s, they will be seeing a larger increase on January 1, 2026. South Dakotans currently earning $11.85, can expect to see a 45-cent rise to $12.30.
 Unlike Nebraska’s amended fixed rate increase, South Dakota’s hourly wage will be adjusted in accordance with the Consumer Price Index (CPI). According to CPI, the average cost of living has risen by 3.7% according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics – slightly above the historical-average.
 Other states raising hourly wages in 2027 include Washington ($17.73), Connecticut ($17.48), California ($17.40), Rhode Island ($17.00), New Jersey ($16.48), Arizona ($15.65), Colorado ($15.71), Maine ($15.70), Michigan ($15.00), Virginia ($13.75), Minnesota ($11.87), Ohio ($11.40), and Montana ($11.20).
